subject: Intermittent API availability affecting Solaris.ai — status page update
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Vega <c.vega@solaris.ai>, ops@solaris.ai
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Intermittent API availability affecting Solaris.ai — status page update

Carlos / Solaris ops team,

We’re seeing an intermittent availability issue that started at ~08:50 PT which may impact some of your inference requests (errors and elevated p50/p95 latency). We’ve opened an incident and have the bridge active; engineering is triaging root cause.

Immediate notes:  
- Scope: a subset of requests routed to us-west edge pop that include long-context chat sessions.
- User impact: increased 5xx and timeouts for ~7% of requests to the hosted text-generation endpoint.
- Mitigation in progress: automated routing fallback to alternative pool and temporary rate limiting for long sessions.

We’ve posted a notice to our status page: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-12-20-solaris-availability (live). I’ll keep this thread updated and share a timeline when we have it.

Attachments: incident-bridge-log.txt (excerpt), statuspage-snapshot.png

Requests from you: please confirm whether you see failed requests in the last 30 minutes for the patterns below (session id prefix: sol-):
- Generation requests with session continuation tokens
- High token-per-request workloads

Thanks and apologies for the disruption — we’ll prioritize your traffic.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Customer Reliability Lead | Redwood Inference
(attachment: incident-bridge-log.txt, text/plain)
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 09:28:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Intermittent API availability affecting Solaris.ai — status page update

Marissa / Evy — short internal update and action items. Forwarding my outbound to Solaris.

Summary for engineering:
- Impact window: ~08:50 PT -> ongoing. Error spike and 3x p95 on some routed requests.
- Suspected vector: KV cache thrashing on long-session requests causing downstream timeouts in the us-west serving pool.
- Current mitigations: routing fallback (partial), rolling config to cap long-session concurrency (in flight), and autoscale in the fallback pool.

Action items:  
- Marissa: update status page to include that fallback routing is active and estimated recovery ETA will be communicated in the next update. Add the note that dedicated customers on reserved capacity are unaffected unless using hosted routing.
- Evy: collect runtime traces and the KV eviction metrics for the window 08:30–09:30 PT, attach to JIRA ENG-4283. Also stash payload samples for further decode.
- Engineering: hold off on model rollouts to us-west for the next 24 hours.

I’ll coordinate externally and request Solaris to share their sample failed request IDs. We should aim to have a clearer customer-facing follow-up within 4–6 hours if we can validate mitigation.

— Hannah
From: Carlos Vega <c.vega@solaris.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@solaris.ai
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Intermittent API availability affecting Solaris.ai — status page update

Thanks Hannah — we see elevated 502/504s starting 08:52 PT that align with what you describe.

Our SRE pulled a handful of request IDs from production (examples below) and included a short stack trace — sending separate secure upload to your ops contact. We’re happy to keep the bridge open and to validate any mitigation you apply.

Example request ids: sol-4f8a, sol-4f8b, sol-4fb2
Observed behavior: timeouts after 12–14s, sometimes partial responses. Clients are retrying which is amplifying load.

Please let us know when routing fallback is fully active so we can resume normal retry policies.

— Carlos Vega
Head of Platform | Solaris.ai
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Vega <c.vega@solaris.ai>, ops@solaris.ai
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 15:40:00 -08:00
Subject: Update: Incident mitigated, next steps and post-incident artifacts

Carlos / Solaris team — final update for today.

What happened (brief): an interaction between long-session KV cache pressure and a recently tightened connection timeouts rule in the us-west serving pool led to transient request failures and elevated tail latency for a subset of long-context sessions. The cascade amplified with client retries.

What we did:  
- Immediately activated routing failover to the us-east fallback pool for affected session patterns.
- Temporarily relaxed the connection timeout threshold while we mitigated the KV eviction behavior.
- Disabled an internal config that increased long-session concurrency on the us-west pool; that config will remain off until we finish the KV eviction fix and a follow-up canary (ENG-4283).

Customer impact: 08:50–14:12 PT for the worst of the failures; by 14:12 PT the fallback routing and timeout tweaks reduced errors to baseline. You may see a small number of delayed requests while client retries clear.

Attachments: incident-bridge-log.txt (full bridge notes), statuspage-snapshot.png (post-update). We’ve also opened a JIRA (JIRA-ENG-4283) for the detailed postmortem; I’ll share the write-up when complete.

Recommended customer next steps:  
- Temporarily reduce aggressive retry backoffs (we recommend exponential backoff starting at 500ms, max 3 retries) while the fix is validated.
- Provide any additional failed request IDs or sample payloads to the secure upload link you used earlier.

We’ll follow up with a formal postmortem and planned remediation timeline by 2026-12-22 EOD. Appreciate the quick coordination and patience.

— Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Customer Reliability Lead | Redwood Inference
